Audit DRG claim MR_05's full coding for this admission — this is ONE determination for the whole stay, not per code, but check every line below (not just the first) since any one of them can drive the claim-level determination.
This claim has 26 billed lines — DO NOT call get_condition_policy on every one of them, and don't run a separate medical-record search per code either; both will overflow the retrieval model's context window well before you reach a determination (verified: this happened on a 19-line claim). retrieval_messages.content:
You are an agent that gathers evidence for a claims audit by querying the
PuppyGraph knowledge graph over Cypher. You receive no pre-fetched context — you must call the
query_puppygraph tool yourself to find evidence, and may call it more than once (e.g. one query
to find a candidate, another to pull supporting detail). Only read Cypher is permitted (no
CREATE/MERGE/DELETE/SET/...).

Graph schema:

Nodes (only the attributes listed are queryable — see "Differences from plain Cypher" below).
Patient, Visit, and Claim are THREE SEPARATE NODE LABELS that all read the SAME physical `visit`
table (Patient filtered to visit_number=1, Claim filtered to claim_id IS NOT NULL, Visit
unfiltered) — each label only exposes ITS OWN attribute list, not the union of all three, even
though the underlying row is identical for a patient's first visit that's also a claim:
  Claim         claim_review_type ('DRG' or 'Readmission', see below), claim_role
                 ('claim' on DRG rows; 'index'/'readmission' on Readmission rows), claim_case_id,
                 claim_index_claim_id, claim_number, claim_payer, claim_admit_date,
                 claim_discharge_date, claim_drg_type, claim_original_drg,
                 claim_original_drg_description, claim_gap_days
                 (claim_facility_name, claim_patient_mrn, claim_patient_name are ONLY populated
                 on the paired READMISSION-role row, never on a DRG or index row — read
                 patient identity via the Patient node instead, see gotcha below; claim_document_list,
                 claim_authorized_days/stay_days/billed_days, claim_total_charges are always
                 null for this review_type. NOTE: there is no `visit_id` attribute on Claim at
                 all — reach the Visit by edge traversal only, see gotcha below)
  Line          claim_id, visit_id, line_type (diagnosis / procedure / drg), position,
                 code_system, code, code_as_billed, description, poa (Y/N), cc, mcc (booleans),
                 document_id (is_principal and diagnosis_type — populated for APC/SNF — are
                 ALWAYS NULL here; position=1 is the only principal-diagnosis signal)
  Code          code_system, code, description
  MedicalRecord visit_id, visit_role, claim_id, doc_kind='medical_record', review_type,
                 file_path, file_name, page_count
  Policy        visit_id, claim_id, doc_kind (coding_guideline / condition_policy /
                 reference_guide), review_type='DRG', file_path, file_name
  Note          document_id, visit_id, day_id, claim_id, review_type, position, note_type,
                 title, section_path, note_date, note_time, author_name, page_start, page_end,
                 text
  Fact          note_id, document_id, visit_id, fact_type, name, row_label, value, number,
                 unit, printed_date, code_id, page_no, quote (not usually needed for DRG —
                 Note.text search covers the same ground; see skills/snf.py if you also
                 need is_measurement/is_service Fact rows, which have a live-verified quirk)
  PolicyRule    document_id, review_type='DRG', doc_kind, rule_type, position, section, label,
                 text, code, code_id, severity (CC/MCC), is_target
  Patient       patient_mrn, patient_date_of_birth, patient_name, patient_name_on_claim,
                 patient_sex, patient_mrn_shared, patient_visit_count — reach it from ANY visit
                 of that patient via reverse HAS_VISIT traversal, see gotcha below
  Day           day_id, visit_id, day_date, day_number, is_admit_day, is_discharge_day,
                 sessions, session_minutes (not usually needed for DRG)

Edges:
  (Claim)-[:HAS_LINE]->(Line)-[:BILLS]->(Code)
  (MedicalRecord)-[:HAS_NOTE]->(Note)-[:STATES]->(Fact)-[:REFERS_TO]->(Code)
  (Policy)-[:HAS_RULE]->(PolicyRule)-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)
  (Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)                -- also traversable in reverse: (Claim)<-[:BILLED_BY]-(Visit)
  (Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)   -- reaches the actual medical record directly,
                                                  filter by review_type (see gotcha below)
  (Visit)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(Visit)              -- current visit -> the PRIOR visit
  (Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)             -- also traversable in reverse from any visit,
                                                  see gotcha below

The 30 DRG claims are MR_01..MR_30; always reach one by `claim_number` alone, e.g.
`MATCH (c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_11'})`. MR_11..MR_30 are Claims with
claim_review_type='DRG'. MR_01..MR_10 are Claims with claim_review_type='Readmission' AND
claim_role='index' — the same stay is also the index (first) admission of one of the 10
index/readmission pairs, and its DRG claim is that index claim. A DRG audit targets the
claim's own coding either way.

Differences from plain Cypher (specific to how this graph was loaded into PuppyGraph):
- CRITICAL: a node's own id (Visit.visit_id, Claim.claim_id, MedicalRecord.document_id, etc.)
  is NOT queryable — not even to re-match that SAME node in a LATER query. If one query gets
  you a Visit via `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'})` and you then
  try `MATCH (v:Visit {visit_id: '<id(v)'s string>'})` in a SEPARATE later query to keep going
  from that visit, it silently returns ZERO rows (verified live on this graph). The fix is to
  do the WHOLE hop chain you need in ONE query, keeping
  every intermediate node as a bound variable in that same query — e.g. `MATCH
  (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}) MATCH
  (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note) WHERE
  toLower(n.text) CONTAINS toLower('pneumonia') RETURN n.title, n.page_start, n.text` as ONE
  query. `id(n)` is for your own inspection only, never something to paste into a later MATCH.
- Every node's OWN primary key (Claim.claim_id, Line.line_id, MedicalRecord/Policy.document_id,
  Note.note_id, Fact.fact_id, PolicyRule.rule_id, Visit.visit_id, Patient.patient_id) is
  consumed into the vertex's internal identity and is NOT itself queryable — `c.claim_id`
  silently returns null. Reach these nodes by EDGE TRAVERSAL, not by matching a reconstructed id
  string.
- RETURNing a whole node (`RETURN c`) comes back as an EMPTY `{}` — always RETURN specific
  properties.
- PATIENT IDENTITY GOTCHA (specific to this graph's Patient/Visit split — verified live):
  v.patient_mrn / v.patient_name on a Visit row come back NULL for every visit except the
  patient's very FIRST one (visit_number=1, the row the Patient node itself reads from) — a DRG
  visit is often not that first visit. Do NOT read patient identity off the Visit
  you're holding; traverse to Patient instead, which works from ANY of that patient's visits in
  either direction: `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:$n}) MATCH
  (p:Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(v) RETURN p.patient_mrn, p.patient_name` (verified live: returns
  the correct MRN/name even when v.patient_mrn itself is null).
- Claim's queryable human identifier is `claim_number` (e.g. 'MR_01'). Claim.claim_index_claim_id
  (queryable, populated on claim_role='readmission' rows only) NAMES the paired index claim's id
  as a string but can't be used to MATCH it directly (target's own id isn't matchable by string
  — see above). To actually reach the index claim/visit from a readmission claim, traverse:
  `(v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(rdm:Claim {claim_number:$rm})`, `(v)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(prevVisit:Visit)`,
  `(prevVisit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(idx:Claim)` — verified live (RM_01's readmission visit
  REVISIT_OF's MR_01's index visit, gap_days=21, matching Claim.claim_gap_days).
- THE KEY GOTCHA THAT STILL APPLIES (a fact about the source data, not a graph-modeling
  artifact): the DRG audit's own supporting content — the index stay's medical record, and every
  condition/coding policy — is loaded as a SEPARATE, PARALLEL copy of MedicalRecord/Note/Fact
  tagged review_type='DRG' (NOT 'Readmission'), even though it documents the exact same claim
  and the exact same PDF. `(Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)` DOES resolve correctly —
  just remember to filter `{review_type:'DRG'}` on the MedicalRecord, since the same Visit also
  has a review_type='Readmission' MedicalRecord pointing at the identical PDF content:
    MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}),
          (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note)
- Code is a shared dimension across ALL review types and code systems (ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS,
  APR-DRG, etc.) — filter by `code_system` too whenever a bare code could collide.
- A code can appear in a DRG condition-policy document TWO different ways, and they can
  DISAGREE on severity — trust the code's own `primary_code` row (reached via
  `(PolicyRule {rule_type:'primary_code'})-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)`), never a `code`-type
  differential mention inside a different concept's document. Always use get_condition_policy
  below rather than hand-writing this traversal.
- Not every billed diagnosis has a governing condition policy — most are untargeted
  comorbidities, not audit concepts.


Domain knowledge for this review type:

DRG claims audit — what this graph is for: a three-way check between what was billed
(Line where line_type IN ['diagnosis','procedure']) on the stay, what the medical record
documents (Note/Fact, reached via the review_type='DRG' MedicalRecord — see the gotcha above),
and what the governing condition/coding policy requires (get_condition_policy below). DRG is
graded per claim (one determination for the whole stay), not per line, but a wrong diagnosis/
procedure/POA/CC-MCC on ANY line can drive that determination — check each targeted line, don't
stop at the first one.

Common DRG Finding categories — use these as hypotheses to check, not a checklist to recite:
- Diagnosis lacks clinical support: code billed but the record doesn't meet the governing
  condition policy's Validation Criteria (e.g. VAP billed with no documented onset timing,
  radiographic infiltrate, or micro/treatment evidence per get_condition_policy's criteria).
  Correction: remove the code (or, if a differential code's criteria ARE met instead, recode
  to it — see CC/MCC severity misclassified below, this is often the same underlying fact
  pattern).
- POA flag wrong: code says present-on-admission but the record's own dated notes show it
  developing during the stay, or vice versa. This is a date-math check — compare the
  condition's documented onset date (Fact.printed_date / Note.note_date) against
  Claim.claim_admit_date — not a keyword search.
- CC/MCC severity misclassified: the billed code's own `primary_code` severity doesn't match
  Line.cc/mcc, OR the record only supports a lower-severity differential code's criteria
  (e.g. J18.9 [CC] documented, not the [MCC] J95.851 VAP-specific criteria) while the higher
  code was billed, or vice versa. Read get_condition_policy's `distinguish` text for the
  billed code — it states exactly which documentation elements separate it from its
  differentials.
- Principal diagnosis sequencing error: every documented diagnosis can be individually
  correctly coded and supported, and the claim can STILL be a Finding if the code in position 1
  isn't the one that actually occasioned the admission per ICD-10-CM sequencing guidelines
  (e.g. a symptom, or a complication that's a manifestation of an already-coded underlying
  condition, billed as principal instead of that underlying condition). Check this SEPARATELY
  from CC/MCC tier and from whether a diagnosis is supported at all — position 1 of
  revised_diagnosis_set is its own binary, ~20%-weighted scoring component (vendor assessment
  doc §3.1.e), distinct from the "Remaining Codes" presence-match component.
- Missing diagnosis: a condition is clearly documented (with its own Validation Criteria met)
  but never appears as a Line at all.
- Duplicate/redundant coding: two Line diagnosis rows capturing the same clinical event.
- Procedure/technique mismatch: the billed ICD-10-PCS procedure code's documented approach/
  duration doesn't match the operative/procedure note.
- Status code left active after resolution: a dependence-status code (ventilator, dialysis,
  etc.) still billed as active when the record shows it resolved before discharge — again a
  date-math check against claim_discharge_date, not a keyword match.
- Missing procedure code: a performed procedure (e.g. "Assistance with respiratory
  ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours") is documented but never coded — distinct
  from a missing diagnosis.

Patient/facility identifiers for a DRG claim are NOT on the Claim node itself, and NOT
reliably on its Visit node either (see SCHEMA's Patient identity gotcha) — traverse
`(Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)` to get them, or, for MR_01..MR_10 only,
look them up on the paired readmission claim.

The medical record for a DRG claim is large (hundreds of Note passages); search on the
specific clinical terms named in the condition policy's Validation Criteria (get_condition_policy
gives you the exact vocabulary — e.g. "endotracheal", "purulent", "PaO2/FiO2") rather than a
generic term.

discharge_disposition (a separate required output field, not one of the Finding categories
above — it's reported on every claim, Finding or not) is the UB-04 patient discharge status:
whether the patient went home or was transferred to another facility (LTACH, acute inpatient
rehab, SNF, etc.), which matters for post-acute-care-transfer payment policy. This is NOT
something to infer from the diagnosis/procedure review above — always call
get_discharge_disposition_note for the claim and report exactly what it says (code and
description, e.g. "63 - Discharged/transferred to LTACH"); null only if it returns no rows.

[p.295] Author: Dr. Ravi Subramanian, MD (Critical Care Medicine)
Date/Time: 2026-02-19 17:00
Location: Medical Intensive Care Unit (MICU 5-West) (admission)
Chief Complaint: "I couldn't get out of bed and my leg hurts terribly."
Triage Acuity ESI 1 (resuscitation)
Arrival EMS, ground
Disposition Admit - ICU
History of Present Illness
[[NAME-0022]] is a 68-year-old man with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus (last A1c 12.4%), hypertension, and diabetic
peripheral neuropathy who presented with three days of severe right thigh pain and swelling, nausea, vomiting, and progressive
weakness. Family notes that the patient had been missing insulin doses for the past week due to depression and was using an SGLT2
inhibitor. On EMS arrival at home, the patient was found obtunded with tachypnea and hypotension. Right thigh was noted to be swollen,
erythematous, and tender with palpable crepitus. Field glucose was 542 mg/dL and ketones were positive. IV fluid resuscitation was
initiated en route. In the ED, the patient was in severe DKA (pH 6.98, bicarbonate 5) and septic shock. CT scan confirmed necrotizing
fasciitis of the right thigh, and emergent surgical consultation was obtained. Broad-spectrum antibiotics including clindamycin for toxin
suppression were initiated.
Past Medical / Surgical History
[p.190] Medical: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with poor control (A1c 12.4%), hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetic peripheral neuropathy,
depression. Surgical: Cholecystectomy remote.
Active Problem List
# | Problem
1 | Severe diabetic ketoacidosis (initial pH 6.98, bicarbonate 5)
2 | Necrotizing fasciitis of right thigh (Type II - Group A Strep + MRSA)
3 | Septic shock with multi-organ dysfunction
4 | Emergency surgical debridement x3 with wound VAC therapy
5 | Split-thickness skin graft to right thigh
6 | Acute respiratory failure with ARDS - resolved
7 | Contrast-induced acute kidney injury (KDIGO 2), non-dialysis
8 | SGLT2-inhibitor-associated euglycemic DKA (contributing factor)
9 | Diabetic ketoacidosis with anion gap 34
10 | Type 2 diabetes mellitus, uncontrolled (A1c 12.4%)
11 | Hypertension
12 | Hyperlipidemia
13 | Diabetic peripheral neuropathy
14 | Post-operative anemia requiring transfusion
15 | ICU-acquired weakness
16 | Post-operative delirium
Social / Family History
Lives alone in apartment. Family (adult daughter) reports concerns about medication compliance and depression. Non-smoker; denies
alcohol or drug abuse. Family history of diabetes.
Review of Systems
Constitutional: weakness, nausea, vomiting. Endocrine: polyuria, polydipsia. Musculoskeletal: severe right thigh pain. Neuro: altered
mental status. Other systems limited by acute presentation.
Physical Examination (on presentation)
Vitals: 39.4 degC | HR 132 | BP 78/45 (MAP 56) | RR 32 | SpO2 92% RA. General: obtunded, diaphoretic, tachypneic (Kussmaul
respirations). HEENT: dry mucous membranes; fruity breath. Cardiac: tachycardic, regular. Respiratory: Kussmaul breathing pattern;
clear bilateral. Abdomen: soft, non-tender. Right thigh: extensive erythema, swelling, and tenderness with palpable crepitus; skin dusky
in areas; sharply demarcated border proximally. Neuro: GCS 11 (E2 V4 M5).
Laboratory Data
WBC 32.4 (with left shift); Hgb 14.2; platelets 285; PT 14.8; Na 128, K 5.8, Cl 92, CO2 5, BUN 42, creatinine 2.4; glucose 542; anion gap
34; beta-hydroxybutyrate 12.2 mmol/L; lactate 8.6 mmol/L; procalcitonin 88.6 ng/mL. Urine ketones 3+. ABG pH 6.98 / PaCO2 12 / PaO2
78 on NRB.
Imaging (Pertinent)
CT Right Thigh with IV Contrast: Necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh with gas in the fascial planes. Chest Radiograph, Portable AP:
No pulmonary abnormalities; support devices appropriately positioned. See the Diagnostic Imaging section for the full report.
Assessment
68-year-old man with poorly controlled T2DM presenting with severe diabetic ketoacidosis (pH 6.98) complicated by necrotizing fasciitis
of the right thigh with septic shock. Requires emergent surgical debridement, aggressive metabolic resuscitation, and multi-organism
antimicrobial coverage.
Plan
1. DKA: insulin infusion 0.1 units/kg/h; aggressive fluid resuscitation; electrolyte replacement per protocol; discontinue SGLT2 inhibitor.
2. Necrotizing fasciitis: emergent surgical debridement; broad-spectrum antimicrobials with clindamycin for toxin suppression; source
control priority.
3. Septic shock: resuscitation to MAP >= 65; norepinephrine and vasopressin; stress-dose steroids if refractory.
4. Respiratory failure: mechanical ventilation; lung-protective settings.
5. AKI: avoid nephrotoxins; renal-dose adjust.
6. Depression/social: psychiatry consultation; family involvement.
7. Prophylaxis: VTE mechanical only until stabilized; stress ulcer.

Admission Orders
Admit: MICU. Condition: critical.
Vitals: continuous telemetry, arterial-line BP, SpO2; hourly assessment; strict I/O.
DKA protocol: normal saline 15-20 mL/kg initial bolus; regular insulin infusion 0.1 units/kg/h; potassium replacement per protocol; hourly
glucose and q2h chemistry.
Ventilation: lung-protective; monitor for ARDS.
Hemodynamics: norepinephrine to MAP >= 65; vasopressin if refractory; steroids if > 0.3 mcg/kg/min norepinephrine.
Antimicrobials: vancomycin + piperacillin-tazobactam + clindamycin (for necrotizing infection - toxin production coverage).
Surgery: STAT general surgery consultation for necrotizing fasciitis; emergent operating room availability.

History of Present Illness (ED)
68-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes presenting with three days of severe right thigh pain, swelling, and systemic symptoms;
missed insulin doses. Found by family obtunded and tachypneic; septic shock and severe DKA identified in the field.
ED Triage / Initial Vitals
39.4 degC | HR 132 | BP 78/45 (MAP 56) | RR 32 | SpO2 92% RA; GCS 11.
Emergency Department Course & Interventions
Sepsis and DKA bundles activated. Aggressive volume resuscitation with normal saline. Insulin infusion initiated. Broad-spectrum
antimicrobials with clindamycin. Emergent CT identified necrotizing fasciitis. Surgical consultation obtained with immediate operating
room availability. Intubation for airway protection and respiratory failure. Vasopressor support with norepinephrine.
ED Medical Decision Making
Life-threatening combination of severe DKA and septic shock from necrotizing fasciitis requiring emergent surgical intervention,
aggressive metabolic resuscitation, and ICU-level care. Multi-disciplinary team activated.
ED Disposition
Emergent transfer to operating room for surgical debridement, then to MICU for continued resuscitation.

[p.979] Attending: Dr. Ravi Subramanian, MD (Critical Care Medicine)
Admit: 2026-02-19 Transfer: 2026-06-06
LOS: 106 days
Reason for Admission: Severe DKA with concurrent necrotizing fasciitis and septic shock.
Admission Diagnoses
Severe diabetic ketoacidosis with necrotizing fasciitis and septic shock
Discharge / Transfer Diagnoses
Resolved severe DKA; resolved necrotizing fasciitis of right thigh status post surgical debridement and STSG; resolved ARDS; resolved
septic shock; contrast-induced AKI with recovery; T2DM (poor control on admission, now improving); hypertension; hyperlipidemia;
diabetic peripheral neuropathy; depression; ICU-acquired weakness.
Hospital Course
[[NAME-0022]] presented with severe diabetic ketoacidosis (pH 6.98) complicated by necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh with septic
shock. Emergent surgical debridement was performed on admission with two additional debridements on ICU days 2 and 4. Deep tissue
cultures grew Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. The course was complicated by
ARDS with successful prone positioning, contrast-induced AKI managed conservatively without RRT, mucus plugging requiring
bronchoscopy, and profound ICU-acquired weakness. Wound care with vacuum-assisted closure was ongoing throughout the stay
followed by successful split-thickness skin graft on ICU day 18 with excellent graft take. Diabetes management was optimized with
endocrinology consultation and the SGLT2 inhibitor was discontinued. The patient is transferred to a long-term acute care hospital for
continued wound care, rehabilitation, and diabetes management.
Physical Examination
Vitals: Tmax 37.2 degC | HR 79 | MAP 76 | RR 15 | SpO2 96%. Airway/Support: conventional nasal cannula, ambulatory. General: Alert,
interactive, comfortable; participating in therapy. HEENT: mucous membranes moist, no scleral icterus. Cardiac: Regular rate and
rhythm; no murmur; well perfused. Respiratory: Clear to diminished; good air movement; tolerating trach collar. Abdomen: soft,
non-distended, +bowel sounds; PEG site clean and dry. Extremities: pulses intact. Neuro: Alert and oriented; CAM-ICU negative;
strength improving with rehab. Skin/Lines: Skin intact; healing well; ambulating with assistance. Right thigh: skin graft in place with
excellent take; healing donor site left thigh.
Laboratory Data (Pertinent)
CBC: WBC 8.0 x103/uL, Hgb 9.9 g/dL, Hct 29%, platelets 224 x109/L (neutrophils 72%). BMP: Na 136, K 4.0, Cl 101, CO2 25, BUN 26,
creatinine 1.18 mg/dL, glucose 159 mg/dL, Ca 8.4, Mg 2.2, Phos 3.6. ABG (07:00): pH 7.37 / PaCO2 37 / PaO2 85 / HCO3 23; lactate
1.2 mmol/L; P/F ratio 297. Markers: procalcitonin 3.2 ng/mL, CRP 27 mg/L, troponin 0.02 ng/mL.
Imaging (Pertinent)
No new imaging obtained today. Most recent radiograph reviewed and compared; findings consistent with the documented clinical
trajectory.
Condition & Functional Status at Transfer
Alert, oriented, and interactive. Nasal cannula 2 L. Ambulating short distances with walker; right lower extremity healing skin graft.
Tolerating diabetic diet. Hemodynamically stable. Blood glucose control improving on insulin regimen. PICC line in place for antibiotic
completion.

Follow-Up & Recommendations
1. Continue LTAC care for wound management and rehabilitation.
2. General Surgery follow-up in 2 weeks for wound assessment.
3. Plastic Surgery follow-up in 2-4 weeks for graft evaluation.
4. Endocrinology follow-up in 2-4 weeks; hemoglobin A1c in 3 months.
5. Infectious Diseases follow-up for antibiotic course completion.
6. Primary Care follow-up for overall management.
7. Psychiatry follow-up for depression treatment.
8. Return precautions: fever, wound problems, blood glucose extremes, chest pain.

Reason for Consultation: Necrotizing fasciitis of right thigh requiring emergent debridement.
History / Impression of Consultant
Consultation requested by the primary care team. Chart reviewed and patient examined at the bedside. Type II necrotizing soft-tissue
infection with rapid progression, hemodynamic instability, and radiographic gas in the soft tissues. LRINEC score elevated. Requires

Documented teaching with teach-back; per-medication education included
[p.653] Clinician Note: Per-medication education is provided at initiation of each new medication and at discharge. Teach-back is documented
for each session. Learning barriers: critical illness and delirium early in the course; participation improved with recovery. Interpreter not
required (English).
Norepinephrine (Levophed)
Purpose Raises blood pressure when the body is in shock.
Dose & Route Titrated via IV infusion to maintain blood pressure.
Side Effects Decreased blood flow to hands/feet; irregular heartbeat.
Monitoring Continuous blood pressure and heart rate monitoring.
Teach-Back Family verbalized understanding that the medicine keeps blood pressure safe.
Vancomycin
Purpose Antibiotic to treat the blood infection (sepsis) and potential MRSA.
Dose & Route Individualized IV dosing based on kidney function and blood levels.
Side Effects Kidney injury (monitored daily); rash if given too fast (Red Man Syndrome).
Monitoring Daily labs; infuse slowly over at least 60 minutes.
Teach-Back Family able to state purpose; instructed to report rash or skin flushing.
Piperacillin-tazobactam (Zosyn)
Purpose Broad-spectrum antibiotic targeting pneumonia and gram-negative bacteria.
Dose & Route 4.5 g IV every 6 hours, extended infusion over 3 hours.
Side Effects Diarrhea; low potassium; allergic reaction (report rash immediately).
Monitoring Renal function, electrolytes daily.
Teach-Back Teach-back deferred - patient sedated. Education provided to son.
Pantoprazole (Protonix)
Purpose Protects the stomach lining while on stress-ulcer prophylaxis.
Dose & Route 40 mg IV once daily, transitioning to oral when tolerating feeds.
Side Effects Low magnesium with long-term use (monitored); headache.
Monitoring Magnesium levels weekly; discontinue at discharge if no indication.
Teach-Back Patient verbalized that medication protects the stomach.
Enoxaparin (Lovenox)
Purpose Blood thinner to prevent blood clots (DVT) in legs and lungs.
Dose & Route Prophylactic dose; adjusted if active clot is confirmed.
Side Effects Bruising at injection site; bleeding (report blood in urine/stool).
[p.904] Monitoring Daily CBC; watch for signs of bleeding.
Teach-Back Son acknowledged understanding of clot-prevention purpose and verbalized when to call
for help (unusual bleeding).
Insulin infusion / Sliding scale
Purpose Controls blood sugar (glucose) which rises during critical illness.
Dose & Route IV infusion titrated to glucose 140-180 mg/dL; transitioned to SC at recovery.
Side Effects
Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia): sweating, confusion, shakiness.
Monitoring Point-of-care glucose every 1-2 hours while on infusion.
Teach-Back Patient able to describe symptoms of low blood sugar at discharge planning.
Amiodarone
Purpose Corrects and prevents rapid irregular heartbeat (atrial fibrillation).
Dose & Route IV load then oral maintenance; dose adjusted per response.
Side Effects Thyroid problems, lung toxicity, liver effects (all monitored). Sensitivity to sunlight - use
sunscreen.
Monitoring Thyroid/liver labs monthly; chest X-ray annually; QT interval on ECG.
Teach-Back Family verbalized that patient needs ongoing monitoring after discharge. Written materials
provided.
Apixaban (Eliquis) - at discharge
Purpose Blood thinner for catheter-associated DVT (blood clot in neck vein).
Dose & Route 10 mg twice daily x 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily x at least 3 months.
Side Effects Increased bleeding risk - avoid NSAIDs, aspirin without physician approval.
Monitoring No routine lab monitoring required, but report unusual bleeding.
Teach-Back Patient and son demonstrated understanding of dose schedule and verbalized to avoid
ibuprofen. Written instruction sheet given.

Hospital Course
[[NAME-0022]] presented with severe diabetic ketoacidosis (pH 6.98) complicated by necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh with septic
shock. Emergent surgical debridement was performed on admission with two additional debridements on ICU days 2 and 4. Deep tissue
cultures grew Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. The course was complicated by
ARDS with successful prone positioning, contrast-induced AKI managed conservatively without RRT, mucus plugging requiring
bronchoscopy, and profound ICU-acquired weakness. Wound care with vacuum-assisted closure was ongoing throughout the stay
followed by successful split-thickness skin graft on ICU day 18 with excellent graft take. Diabetes management was optimized with
endocrinology consultation and the SGLT2 inhibitor was discontinued. The patient is transferred to a long-term acute care hospital for
continued wound care, rehabilitation, and diabetes management.

Vitals: Tmax 37.2 degC | HR 79 | MAP 76 | RR 15 | SpO2 96%. Airway/Support: conventional nasal cannula, ambulatory. General: Alert,
interactive, comfortable; participating in therapy. HEENT: mucous membranes moist, no scleral icterus. Cardiac: Regular rate and
rhythm; no murmur; well perfused. Respiratory: Clear to diminished; good air movement; tolerating trach collar. Abdomen: soft,
non-distended, +bowel sounds; PEG site clean and dry. Extremities: pulses intact. Neuro: Alert and oriented; CAM-ICU negative;
strength improving with rehab. Skin/Lines: Skin intact; healing well; ambulating with assistance. Right thigh: skin graft in place with
excellent take; healing donor site left thigh.

judge_messages.content:
You are a senior clinical claims auditor deciding a determination for one
billed claim line. You are given, below, everything a retrieval step already queried from a
claims/medical-record/policy knowledge graph for this line — the Cypher queries run and the
rows each one returned. You have no tool access and cannot query further; decide only from
what's shown.

Domain knowledge for this review type:

DRG claims audit — what this graph is for: a three-way check between what was billed
(Line where line_type IN ['diagnosis','procedure']) on the stay, what the medical record
documents (Note/Fact, reached via the review_type='DRG' MedicalRecord — see the gotcha above),
and what the governing condition/coding policy requires (get_condition_policy below). DRG is
graded per claim (one determination for the whole stay), not per line, but a wrong diagnosis/
procedure/POA/CC-MCC on ANY line can drive that determination — check each targeted line, don't
stop at the first one.

Common DRG Finding categories — use these as hypotheses to check, not a checklist to recite:
- Diagnosis lacks clinical support: code billed but the record doesn't meet the governing
  condition policy's Validation Criteria (e.g. VAP billed with no documented onset timing,
  radiographic infiltrate, or micro/treatment evidence per get_condition_policy's criteria).
  Correction: remove the code (or, if a differential code's criteria ARE met instead, recode
  to it — see CC/MCC severity misclassified below, this is often the same underlying fact
  pattern).
- POA flag wrong: code says present-on-admission but the record's own dated notes show it
  developing during the stay, or vice versa. This is a date-math check — compare the
  condition's documented onset date (Fact.printed_date / Note.note_date) against
  Claim.claim_admit_date — not a keyword search.
- CC/MCC severity misclassified: the billed code's own `primary_code` severity doesn't match
  Line.cc/mcc, OR the record only supports a lower-severity differential code's criteria
  (e.g. J18.9 [CC] documented, not the [MCC] J95.851 VAP-specific criteria) while the higher
  code was billed, or vice versa. Read get_condition_policy's `distinguish` text for the
  billed code — it states exactly which documentation elements separate it from its
  differentials.
- Principal diagnosis sequencing error: every documented diagnosis can be individually
  correctly coded and supported, and the claim can STILL be a Finding if the code in position 1
  isn't the one that actually occasioned the admission per ICD-10-CM sequencing guidelines
  (e.g. a symptom, or a complication that's a manifestation of an already-coded underlying
  condition, billed as principal instead of that underlying condition). Check this SEPARATELY
  from CC/MCC tier and from whether a diagnosis is supported at all — position 1 of
  revised_diagnosis_set is its own binary, ~20%-weighted scoring component (vendor assessment
  doc §3.1.e), distinct from the "Remaining Codes" presence-match component.
- Missing diagnosis: a condition is clearly documented (with its own Validation Criteria met)
  but never appears as a Line at all.
- Duplicate/redundant coding: two Line diagnosis rows capturing the same clinical event.
- Procedure/technique mismatch: the billed ICD-10-PCS procedure code's documented approach/
  duration doesn't match the operative/procedure note.
- Status code left active after resolution: a dependence-status code (ventilator, dialysis,
  etc.) still billed as active when the record shows it resolved before discharge — again a
  date-math check against claim_discharge_date, not a keyword match.
- Missing procedure code: a performed procedure (e.g. "Assistance with respiratory
  ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours") is documented but never coded — distinct
  from a missing diagnosis.

Patient/facility identifiers for a DRG claim are NOT on the Claim node itself, and NOT
reliably on its Visit node either (see SCHEMA's Patient identity gotcha) — traverse
`(Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)` to get them, or, for MR_01..MR_10 only,
look them up on the paired readmission claim.

The medical record for a DRG claim is large (hundreds of Note passages); search on the
specific clinical terms named in the condition policy's Validation Criteria (get_condition_policy
gives you the exact vocabulary — e.g. "endotracheal", "purulent", "PaO2/FiO2") rather than a
generic term.

discharge_disposition (a separate required output field, not one of the Finding categories
above — it's reported on every claim, Finding or not) is the UB-04 patient discharge status:
whether the patient went home or was transferred to another facility (LTACH, acute inpatient
rehab, SNF, etc.), which matters for post-acute-care-transfer payment policy. This is NOT
something to infer from the diagnosis/procedure review above — always call
get_discharge_disposition_note for the claim and report exactly what it says (code and
description, e.g. "63 - Discharged/transferred to LTACH"); null only if it returns no rows.


Decide per the three-way check: does the medical record, read against what the governing
policy actually requires, support the billed code? Read the documentation text carefully and
literally rather than pattern-matching on a surface word — e.g. a procedure documented as
"partial" (a partial meniscectomy, a partial tonsillectomy) is often the correct, complete,
billable term for a specific technique, not evidence that something was left incomplete; check
what the policy's own criteria actually turn on before concluding a word like "partial" means
the billed code wasn't met.

Set determination to "Insufficient Evidence" rather than guessing if what's retrieved doesn't
support a real decision either way — do not invent a Finding/No Finding to fill the gap.

system_note is the auditor note a human reviewer reads on EVERY claim, Finding or not — write
it with explicit citations (document/section/page) and reasoning a reviewer could audit line by
line; a correct determination with a
vague, citation-free note still scores as a weak note (see the quality bar in the schema
field's own description).

rationale_letter is a SEPARATE, formal appeal-ready letter to the provider — only written when
determination is Finding (null otherwise). It restates the finding and its basis for an
external, non-technical reader, not a repeat of system_note's internal auditor reasoning.

Page numbers: a medical-record note can span several PDF pages, and its page_start/page_end
are not the page of any particular line in it. In a long note's text, a [p.N] marker means the
text after it (up to the next marker) is on physical page N; cite that page in system_note,
never a note's page_start/page_end range. A note whose page_start equals its page_end is all on
that page. In a multi-page note with no marker before the line, name the note without a page.

evidence_cited must reference only passages that actually appear in the retrieved rows above.
Each entry is the source_id of the one row the quote comes from, copied exactly, and the quote
copied verbatim from that row's text, character for character: don't wrap part of it in
quotation marks, fix a typo, or drop a word or code from the middle. Never invent or recall one. Code checks each quote
against that row and fills in the document, section and page from it, so a quote that isn't in
the cited row, or a source_id that wasn't retrieved, is dropped. Each quote is ONE contiguous
passage from a single row: if you need two separate passages, give two separate evidence_cited
entries rather than joining them with "..."; a stitched-together quote can't be verified. Rows
with no source_id (claim lines, code descriptions, a tool's own summary rows) aren't citable;
cite the record or policy row behind them instead.

Patient name, MRN, and date of birth appear as de-identification tokens like [[MRN-0046]] —
including inline inside quoted note/fact text — not real values. Reproduce them exactly as
given in system_note, rationale_letter, and evidence_cited quotes; a separate step restores
the real values afterward. Never remark on the token format or guess/reconstruct what it stands
for.

discharge_disposition, finding_reason, recovery_type, skilled_services,
adjusted_date_of_service, corrected_revenue_code, adjusted_units_billed,
revised_diagnosis_set, and revised_procedure_set are only meaningful for specific review types
(DRG, Readmission, SNF, SNF, SNF, SNF, DRG, and DRG respectively) — see each field's own schema
description and this review type's domain notes above to know whether to populate it; leave it
null when this review type doesn't call for it.

If this is a DRG review: you are deciding for the WHOLE claim in one pass, not one line — check
every diagnosis and procedure line given to you (POA, CC/MCC tier, whether it's still
supported), not just the one the question happens to name first. revised_diagnosis_set and
revised_procedure_set must each be the claim's COMPLETE corrected list (every code that should
remain billed, in the same shape as what you were given, position 1 = principal diagnosis) —
not a delta of only the line(s) that changed. code_decisions is what's scored: one entry per
billed code, each exactly once, plus additions, with the POA and CC/MCC tier each diagnosis
should carry, and the evidence_cited IDs behind every change. Code checks it and builds the
corrected lists from it.

Teach-back is documented\nfor each session. Learning barriers: critical illness and delirium early in the course; participation improved with recovery. Interpreter not\nrequired (English).\nNorepinephrine (Levophed)\nPurpose Raises blood pressure when the body is in shock.\nDose & Route Titrated via IV infusion to maintain blood pressure.\nSide Effects Decreased blood flow to hands/feet; irregular heartbeat.\nMonitoring Continuous blood pressure and heart rate monitoring.\nTeach-Back Family verbalized understanding that the medicine keeps blood pressure safe.\nVancomycin\nPurpose Antibiotic to treat the blood infection (sepsis) and potential MRSA.\nDose & Route Individualized IV dosing based on kidney function and blood levels.\nSide Effects Kidney injury (monitored daily); rash if given too fast (Red Man Syndrome).\nMonitoring Daily labs; infuse slowly over at least 60 minutes.\nTeach-Back Family able to state purpose; instructed to report rash or skin flushing.\nPiperacillin-tazobactam (Zosyn)\nPurpose Broad-spectrum antibiotic targeting pneumonia and gram-negative bacteria.\nDose & Route 4.5 g IV every 6 hours, extended infusion over 3 hours.\nSide Effects Diarrhea; low potassium; allergic reaction (report rash immediately).\nMonitoring Renal function, electrolytes daily.\nTeach-Back Teach-back deferred - patient sedated. Education provided to son.\nPantoprazole (Protonix)\nPurpose Protects the stomach lining while on stress-ulcer prophylaxis.\nDose & Route 40 mg IV once daily, transitioning to oral when tolerating feeds.\nSide Effects Low magnesium with long-term use (monitored); headache.\nMonitoring Magnesium levels weekly; discontinue at discharge if no indication.\nTeach-Back Patient verbalized that medication protects the stomach.\nEnoxaparin (Lovenox)\nPurpose Blood thinner to prevent blood clots (DVT) in legs and lungs.\nDose & Route Prophylactic dose; adjusted if active clot is confirmed.\nSide Effects Bruising at injection site; bleeding (report blood in urine/stool).\n[p.904] Monitoring Daily CBC; watch for signs of bleeding.\nTeach-Back Son acknowledged understanding of clot-prevention purpose and verbalized when to call\nfor help (unusual bleeding).\nInsulin infusion / Sliding scale\nPurpose Controls blood sugar (glucose) which rises during critical illness.\nDose & Route IV infusion titrated to glucose 140-180 mg/dL; transitioned to SC at recovery.\nSide Effects\nLow blood sugar (hypoglycemia): sweating, confusion, shakiness.\nMonitoring Point-of-care glucose every 1-2 hours while on infusion.\nTeach-Back Patient able to describe symptoms of low blood sugar at discharge planning.\nAmiodarone\nPurpose Corrects and prevents rapid irregular heartbeat (atrial fibrillation).\nDose & Route IV load then oral maintenance; dose adjusted per response.\nSide Effects Thyroid problems, lung toxicity, liver effects (all monitored). Sensitivity to sunlight - use\nsunscreen.\nMonitoring Thyroid/liver labs monthly; chest X-ray annually; QT interval on ECG.\nTeach-Back Family verbalized that patient needs ongoing monitoring after discharge. Written materials\nprovided.\nApixaban (Eliquis) - at discharge\nPurpose Blood thinner for catheter-associated DVT (blood clot in neck vein).\nDose & Route 10 mg twice daily x 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily x at least 3 months.\nSide Effects Increased bleeding risk - avoid NSAIDs, aspirin without physician approval.\nMonitoring No routine lab monitoring required, but report unusual bleeding.\nTeach-Back Patient and son demonstrated understanding of dose schedule and verbalized to avoid\nibuprofen. result.system_note: What was billed: Principal M72.6 (Necrotizing fasciitis) [POA=Y, MCC], plus R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) [POA=Y, MCC], organism lines A49.59 / A49.02 / B95.62, J96.01/J80 for respiratory failure/ARDS, multiple diabetes codes, AKI (N17.9), and procedures including emergent debridement, ETT insertion, prolonged ventilation, PICC/central line insertion, and a billed 0HRJX73 (replacement of right upper leg skin with autologous tissue substitute, full thickness). What the record documents (key citations): H&P and ED/consult notes document CT-confirmed necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh with palpable crepitus and emergent operative management (History & Physical; Emergency Dept note; General Surgery consult): CT scan confirmed necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh, and emergent surgical consultation was obtained (History & Physical, p.295) [ev1]; Type II necrotizing soft-tissue infection with rapid progression, hemodynamic instability, and radiographic gas in the soft tissues (General Surgery Consult, p.379) [ev2]; and the ICU/attending notes state emergent surgical debridement was performed with extensive tissue removal to fascia and that the patient had septic shock requiring vasopressors and was intubated for respiratory failure (Critical Care Progress Note, p.216) [ev3]. Deep tissue cultures identified Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (Infectious Diseases consult, p.172) [ev4]. The discharge summary documents multiple debridements and a split-thickness skin graft (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.979) [ev11]. What the governing policies require (key citations): Coding M72.6 (necrotizing fasciitis, MCC) requires provider documentation of confirmed necrotizing fasciitis plus operative or imaging confirmation of fascial-plane involvement or the presumption rules for transferred operative confirmation (Necrotizing Fasciitis policy - Validation Criteria: Criterion 1 requires provider documentation of 'necrotizing fasciitis' in operative or attending/ID notes; Criterion 3 requires at least one operative finding such as gross fascial necrosis) [ev5, ev6]. The Sepsis policy requires that severe sepsis / septic shock (R65.21) be supported by documentation of septic shock (vasopressor use + lactate criteria or explicit physician documentation of septic shock) and, when an organism is identified, that the appropriate organism-specific sepsis code (A40.- or A41.-) be assigned (Sepsis policy: vasopressor documentation and lactate criteria; and organism -> A40/A41 mapping) [ev7, ev8, ev9, ev10]. Assessment tying record to policy and findings: - Necrotizing fasciitis (M72.6): Supported. CT imaging showing gas in fascial planes and operative debridement with tissue removal to fascia meet the policy's Validation Criteria (operative confirmation or imaging) for M72.6. Evidence: CT-confirmation and emergent operative debridement (History & Physical p.295 [ev1]; General Surgery consult p.379 [ev2]; Critical Care Progress Note p.216 [ev3]; Necrotizing Fasciitis policy requirements [ev5, ev6]). Keep M72.6 as an MCC-level diagnosis and POA=Y is supported by documentation that these findings were present on initial presentation. - Severe sepsis with septic shock (R65.21): Supported clinically (documented septic shock with vasopressors and elevated lactate in progress notes: see Critical Care Progress Note showing vasopressors and ABG/lactate and P/F ratio consistent with organ dysfunction) and appropriately MCC-level under policy [ev3; ev7; ev8]. R65.21 as an additional diagnosis is supported, POA=Y is consistent with documentation of shock on admission. - Organism coding / sequencing error (Finding): The medical record documents identified organisms (deep tissue cultures grew Streptococcus pyogenes [Group A] and MRSA) [ev4]. The Sepsis policy explicitly maps identified organisms to organism-specific sepsis codes (e.g., Group A Streptococcus -> A40.0; Staphylococcus aureus - MRSA -> A41.02) and instructs coders to use A40.- / A41.- when the organism is identified rather than non-sepsis organism codes (Sepsis policy organism table) [ev9, ev10]. This claim instead lists A49.59 / A49.02 and B95.62 (other/unspecified streptococcal infection and MRSA as cause) while also coding R65.21. That combination does not follow the policy pathway for documented sepsis with identified organism: when an organism causing sepsis is identified, the appropriate A40.- or A41.- sepsis code should be assigned (and R65.21 reported as additional), rather than A49.- / B95.x organism/unspecified-site codes alone. Therefore the organism/sepsis coding is misclassified and must be corrected (remove A49.59 / A49.02 / B95.62 and substitute the appropriate organism-specific sepsis code(s)). Evidence: cultures positive for Group A Strep and MRSA (Infectious Diseases consult p.172) [ev4]; policy mapping (Group A -> A40.0; MRSA -> A41.02) [ev9, ev10]. - Procedure technique mismatch (Finding): The discharge and procedure documentation document a split-thickness skin graft (STSG) on ICU day 18 with excellent graft take (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.979) [ev11], while the billed PCS 0HRJX73 describes replacement with an autologous tissue substitute, full thickness. The record supports a split-thickness graft rather than a full-thickness autologous tissue substitute as billed; coding should be changed to the correct PCS for a split-thickness skin graft (or removed/recoded) - physician/coding clarification required. Evidence: discharge summary documents split-thickness skin graft (p.979) [ev11]. Other diagnoses and procedures (respiratory failure, ARDS, AKI, DKA, prolonged ventilation, central line/PICC, platelet transfusion, diabetes comorbidities): clinically supported by H&P, ICU notes, nephrology and ID consults and discharge summary (examples: severe DKA pH 6.98 [History & Physical, p.295] [ev13]; ABG/lactate and P/F ratio consistent with respiratory failure/ARDS [Critical Care Progress Note, p.216] [ev12]; nephrology consult documenting AKI peak and conservative management [NOTE n43]; discharge summary documenting course and recovery) and may be kept as billed. The prolonged ventilation/procedure 5A1D90Z is supported by early intubation for respiratory failure, ARDS, and extended ICU course (intubation on admission + ARDS and very low P/F) though the precise >96-hour documentation that coders require should be verified in ICU flow sheets; we cite the sustained ARDS/intubation and long ICU stay as clinical support (Critical Care Progress Note p.216; Discharge Summary p.979) [ev3, ev11]. Summary of changes required (high-level): 1) Remove the non-sepsis organism codes (A49.59, A49.02, B95.62) and replace with the appropriate organism-specific sepsis code(s) (A40.0 and/or A41.02) to pair properly with R65.21 per the Sepsis policy (evidence: culture results and policy mapping) [ev4, ev9, ev10]. 2) Clarify principal-diagnosis sequencing (whether principal should remain M72.6 or whether organism-specific sepsis (A40/A41) should be principal given R65.21) - documentation supports M72.6 as the operative, source-control diagnosis, but Sepsis policy favors A40/A41 pairing with R65.21 when sepsis is the primary reason for admission; this sequencing decision requires coder/physician clarification. 3) Remove or recode PCS 0HRJX73 (billed as full-thickness autologous tissue replacement) because the record documents a split-thickness skin graft (Discharge Summary p.979) [ev11]; replace with the correct PCS for split-thickness graft after physician/operative note confirmation. Evidence cited (by id): ev1, ev2, ev3, ev4, ev5, ev6, ev7, ev8, ev9, ev10, ev11. result.rationale_letter: Dear Provider/Coding Team, Re: MR_05 (Admit 02/19/2026-Discharge/Transfer 06/06/2026) - Audit Finding: Sepsis/organism coding and one procedure technique mismatch We reviewed the full inpatient record (History & Physical, Critical Care notes, General Surgery consult, Infectious Diseases consult, and Discharge/Transfer Summary) against our DRG coding policies. The audit identified two issues that require correction: 1) Sepsis/organism coding does not follow policy for documented organism-specific sepsis. Basis: Deep tissue cultures identified Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (Infectious Diseases consult, 02/21/2026) [ev4]. Our Sepsis policy requires that when a causative organism is identified for sepsis, an organism-specific sepsis code from A40.- or A41.- is assigned (examples: Group A Streptococcus -> A40.0; MRSA -> A41.02) and R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) is coded as an additional code per policy mapping [ev9, ev10]. The claim billed A49.59 / A49.02 and B95.62 for the organisms while also billing R65.21. Per policy, the appropriate action when cultures identify the sepsis organism is to assign the organism-specific sepsis code (A40.- / A41.-) rather than non-sepsis organism-site codes alone. Therefore we are removing A49.59 / A49.02 / B95.62 and will assign the appropriate organism-specific sepsis code(s) in their place, pending final physician/coder determination of which organism is the primary sepsis etiology (see HITL question below). 2) Procedure technique mismatch - skin graft type: Basis: The discharge summary documents a split-thickness skin graft on ICU day 18 with excellent graft take (Discharge / Transfer Summary, 06/06/2026) [ev11]. The billed PCS 0HRJX73 describes replacement of right upper leg skin with autologous tissue substitute, full thickness. The clinical documentation supports a split-thickness skin graft (STSG), not a full-thickness autologous replacement as billed; this requires recoding to the correct ICD-10-PCS code for STSG or removal/replacement depending on the operative note. Please provide the operative report that documents the graft thickness and technique so coding may be corrected. What we are changing now (audit correction to be applied unless provider supplies clarifying documentation within the appeal period): - Remove A49.59 (other streptococcal infection), A49.02 (MRSA infection, unspecified site), and B95.62 (MRSA as cause of disease elsewhere) and add the appropriate organism-specific sepsis code(s) (A40.0 and/or A41.02) paired with R65.21, consistent with the Sepsis policy. Evidence: deep tissue cultures positive for Group A Strep and MRSA (ID consult) and policy organism mapping (Sepsis policy) [ev4, ev9, ev10]. - Remove procedure 0HRJX73 (replacement with autologous tissue substitute, full thickness) and recode to the appropriate PCS reflecting a split-thickness skin graft after review of the operative report/skin-graft operative note (Discharge summary documents STSG on ICU day 18) [ev11]. Requested documentation to resolve outstanding items (please supply within 30 days): 1. Operative report(s) for the index debridement(s) and the skin graft procedure that document whether the graft was split-thickness versus full-thickness and the exact graft technique/materials used. (Needed to assign correct PCS code in place of 0HRJX73.) 2. Clarification from the operative/surgical or infectious disease team as to which organism should be coded as the organism responsible for sepsis when multiple organisms grew (Group A Streptococcus vs MRSA), or documentation that sepsis was polymicrobial and how you want it reflected in coded sepsis (A40.0 vs A41.02 vs combination). This will determine whether A40.0 or A41.02 (or both) should be used and whether sepsis should be sequenced principal vs secondary. If no additional documentation is provided, the claim-level corrections described above will be applied: remove A49.59/A49.02/B95.62; add organism-specific sepsis code(s) per ID culture results (A40.0 and/or A41.02) paired with R65.21; remove 0HRJX73 and recode OR mark for recoding pending operative report. Sincerely, Clinical Claims Audit Team Key evidence cited: History & Physical (admit H&P) and surgical/ICU notes documenting CT and operative debridement of necrotizing fasciitis [ev1, ev2, ev3]; Infectious Diseases consult documenting Group A Streptococcus and MRSA growth [ev4]; Necrotizing Fasciitis policy Validation Criteria (operative confirmation requirement) [ev5, ev6]; Sepsis policy vasopressor/lactate and organism-to-sepsis-code mapping (A40.0 / A41.02) [ev7, ev8, ev9, ev10]; Discharge summary documenting STSG [ev11].
